svg.title: Why the payment path fails static rather than closed
svg.desc: A timeline in hours. The payment-path credential holds an eight-hour lease. The broker outage it has to survive is the four-hour recovery target, which is unvalidated until the disaster recovery drill measures it. The four hours between them are margin for detecting a renewal failure and getting a human to it. A dashed ceiling stands at twenty-four hours: if a measured recovery time ever required a longer lease than that, the recovery time gets fixed rather than the lease extended. Below the timeline, the current state is a hardcoded, shared, unrotated password with no attribution and no revocation path, against a brokered credential that is unique per workload, tied to a lease identifier, attributable and revocable. Two kill paths exist that do not transit the broker: a dual-authorised out-of-band DBA runbook, and a sealed break-glass credential under a two-of-three quorum with regulator notification inside four hours.
svg.text: Payments fail static, not closed — the lease outlives the outage
24h ceiling — above this, fix the RTO instead
Payment-path credential · 8h TTL · renewed every 30 minutes
Broker outage it has to survive · 4h RTO — target, unvalidated until the DR drill
4h margin — detect the renewal failure, get a human to it
Unattributed in any log, in a file on a server
Unique per workload, tied to a lease ID
Attributable, revocable, expires on its own
KILL CAPABILITY THAT DOES NOT TRANSIT THE BROKER
two authorised DBAs · SIEM alarm · quarterly attestation
two of three quorum · regulator notified inside 4h
